kernel.strategy: vendor-downstream required; exact source not yet acquired
kernel.source: no approved source: community recovery configuration is evidence only; obtain exact Samsung GPL release before integration

runtime.architecture_evidence: config.gz (2026-10-17): header Linux/arm64, CONFIG_ARM64=y, CONFIG_COMPAT=y. The 'armv8l' from uname is what a 32-bit process sees on an arm64 kernel, not the kernel's own architecture. armv7 userspace is kept for memory footprint and parity with the stock 32-bit userspace; an aarch64 userspace is possible on this kernel but is not selected (ADR 0002).

boot.unlock_status: OEM-unlock availability verified on the unit by the maintainer (2026-10-13): the toggle exists and unlocking is possible; the 2026-10-08 capture showed sys.oem_unlock_allowed=0 before the toggle was used. Whether the bootloader is actually unlocked is not recorded (unlocking erases user data and trips Knox).

known_limitations: The exact running kernel version is confirmed, but the matching Samsung GPL source, kernel image, DTB, and kernel configuration have not been acquired.
OEM unlock is available (maintainer-verified) but the bootloader unlock itself has not been recorded as performed; no boot image has been written to the device.
No boot, kernel, display, input, storage, Wi-Fi, suspend, or recovery result has been validated on hardware.
This profile is a source-of-truth record of evidence gaps, not a flashable device port.
